expectations.text: Treats the 3 versus 4 issue count as author confirmation because duplicate or overlapping scope is possible
expectations.evidence: The baseline asks whether the categories overlap and says not to form a final rewrite before confirming the counting scope.

expectations.text: Identifies the contradiction between two issues still open and all residual issues resolved
expectations.evidence: The opening judgment and confirmation questions explicitly identify the conflict between two open issues and all residual issues resolved.

expectations.text: Compares how project, product, and non-testing readers may interpret resolved versus continue to follow up
expectations.evidence: The baseline mentions possible role interpretations inside a problem table, but it does not independently restate and compare project-manager, product/business, and non-testing-reader understandings of resolved versus follow-up status.

expectations.text: Pauses final factual revision until the author clarifies issue-count scope and current status
expectations.evidence: The baseline explicitly withholds a final factual rewrite until the author confirms the total, category relation, and state.

expectations.text: Provides safe suggested wording or placeholders without silently choosing a count
expectations.evidence: The baseline provides recommendations and an organization order but no safe replacement wording or placeholder-based revision that the author could use after clarification.

expectations.text: Avoids repeating the same root issue across multiple long sections
expectations.evidence: The 39-line baseline is concise and keeps each root issue primarily in one table row, with confirmation questions separated.
